execution: single-use correctness canary with checkpointed one-shot evidence collection
methodRevision: The prior v2 canary discarded its successful first asynchronous evidence snapshot, rendered and captured its screenshot, and then timed out in a second asynchronous snapshot. V3 retains the first snapshot, requests shader compilation info exactly once, and uses only a synchronous late-state read after the screenshot.

priorAttempt.relationship: method revision after an inconclusive harness timeout; not an independent confirmation or replacement

assertions: the prior v2 report, checksum sidecar, and screenshot remain byte-identical to their frozen identities
the candidate working diff is byte-identical to the frozen patch
the ordinary renderer path owns the sole adapter and device acquisition
the acquired adapter reports that it is not a fallback adapter
the actual device reports maxImmediateSize at least four and the WGSL language feature is present
one immediate and one ordinary scene pipeline render eight indexed BatchedMesh commands each, followed by the expected ordinary output-transform draw
immediate setters carry exact uint32 ordinals zero through seven immediately before their draws
the ordinary batch emits no immediate setter
the immediate WGSL requirement and declaration compile without messages and compilation info is requested exactly once per shader module
all WebGPU validation scopes are balanced, settled, and empty
the deterministic example reaches phase three and both actual BatchedMesh command lists equal the expected order
raw synchronous page and GPU state is written to an immutable pre-collection checkpoint before any asynchronous diagnostic wait
the successful initial GPU snapshot is written to an immutable checkpoint before screenshot or late-state work
late page and GPU state is read synchronously after all postflight work and is deeply identical to the initial snapshot
browser, page, GPU, network, and harness-teardown diagnostics are empty
a full-resolution screenshot is captured for visual inspection
claimBoundary: Correctness and integration on one Chrome/WebGPU implementation using Three-owned device acquisition; no performance or cross-device universality claim. The prior v2 run remains an inconclusive harness timeout and is not erased by this method revision.
